units.sourceHTML: 18.1.1 Handling Multi-byte and Varying-Width Characters

units.text: ⟦0⟧, ⟦1⟧ and ⟦2⟧ treat each line of input as a string of characters and encoding errors, where an ⟦3⟧encoding error⟦4⟧ is an input byte that is not part of any character. Single-byte and multi-byte characters are supported, along with common character encoding systems like UTF-8. The operating system’s locale specifies the character encoding, and can be specified with the ⟦5⟧ environment variable. You can find which locales are supported on your system by running the shell command ‘⟦6⟧’.
units.sourceHTML: diff, diff3 and sdiff treat each line of input as a string of characters and encoding errors, where an encoding error is an input byte that is not part of any character. Single-byte and multi-byte characters are supported, along with common character encoding systems like UTF-8. The operating system’s locale specifies the character encoding, and can be specified with the LC_ALL environment variable. You can find which locales are supported on your system by running the shell command ‘locale -a’.

units.text: When counting columns for options like ⟦0⟧ (⟦1⟧), ⟦2⟧ consults the locale for the column width of each character, and assumes that each encoding error occupies a single column.
units.sourceHTML: When counting columns for options like --expand-tabs (-t), diff consults the locale for the column width of each character, and assumes that each encoding error occupies a single column.

units.text: When ignoring case for ⟦0⟧ (⟦1⟧), ⟦2⟧ downcases each character before comparing it, regardless of whether it is multi-byte. See ⟦3⟧Suppressing Case Differences⟦4⟧.
units.sourceHTML: When ignoring case for --ignore-case (-i), diff downcases each character before comparing it, regardless of whether it is multi-byte. See Suppressing Case Differences.
